## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **GitHub polling needs an allowlist.** New host-only `github.polling_repositories = ["owner/repo", ...]`; empty (the default) ignores every notification, so polling deployments must set it (#4294).
- **Jira `project_keys = []` now disables lookups.** The default is now `["*"]`. If you set `[]` to mean "all projects", change it to `["*"]` or remove it (#4049).
- **`litellm.extra_headers` is host-only.** Repository `.pr_agent.toml` and comment arguments can no longer set it (#4287).
- **Default model is now `gpt-6.1-sol`** with `gpt-6-luna` as fallback (was `gpt-5.6` / `gpt-5.6-terra`). Pin `config.model` to keep the old one (#4088).
- **Langfuse SDK 4.18.0** needs self-hosted Langfuse 3.63.0+; use the `langfuse_otel` callback (#4343).
- **GitHub App token in Actions:** set `github.agent_login` to `<app-slug>[bot]` so PR-Agent recognises its own comments (#4329).

## ✨ Highlights

- `pr-agent doctor` preflights a deployment (#4321).
- `--json-output` for `/describe`, `/improve` and `/review` (#4265, #4227, #4226).
- Jira scoped API tokens (#4250), `/ask` with the CI artifact as context (#4176), globs in `repo_context_files` (#4220), opt-in GitLab subgroup settings inheritance (#4059).
- Security hardening: DNS rebinding block, repo-context path escapes, host-only config output, loguru diagnose off, more credential redaction (#4252, #4279, #4293, #4280, #4328).

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes > [!WARNING] > This release changes several defaults and makes more settings host-only. Check each item below against your deployment before upgrading. - **`pip install pr-agent` no longer installs the git provider SDKs** ([#3679](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3679)): PyGithub, python-gitlab, atlassian-python-api, the Azure DevOps SDKs, boto3, giteapy, the Google Cloud SDKs and a2a-sdk moved to the `github`, `gitlab`, `bitbucket`, `azure`, `codecommit`, `gitea`, `google` and `mosaico` extras. Install the ones you use, for example `pip install "pr-agent[github]"`, or `pr-agent[all]` for the previous set. The Docker images already install `all`. - **Docker service images run as a non-root user** ([#3910](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3910)): the webhook, app, polling and Mosaico targets run as UID/GID `10001` with `HOME=/home/pragent`. Mounted secrets must be readable by that user, output and database directories must be writable, and home-relative mounts should move to `/home/pragent`. The GitHub Action, CLI and Lambda images still run as root. - **Azure DevOps and Bitbucket Server webhooks require credentials** ([#3911](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3911)): with `azure_devops_server.webhook_username`/`webhook_password` or `bitbucket_server.webhook_secret` unset, every webhook is rejected with HTTP 403. Set them on both the sender and PR-Agent before upgrading. - **GitLab webhooks backed by a secret provider need a new token format** ([#3913](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3913)): when GitLab credentials come from AWS Secrets Manager or Google Cloud Storage, the webhook's Secret Token must be `:`. Name-only tokens are rejected with HTTP 401, so update the webhooks when you deploy. - **Namespace-wide settings are off by default** ([#3908](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3908)): PR-Agent no longer applies `/pr-agent-settings` to every repository automatically. Set the host-only `config.global_settings_repo = "pr-agent-settings"` to keep the old behaviour. - **`[tool.pr-agent]` in `pyproject.toml` is no longer read** ([#3941](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3941)): move those settings to `.pr_agent.toml`. - **More settings are host-only** ([#3840](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3840), [#3904](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3904), [#3950](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3950), [#4001](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/4001), [#4054](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/4054)): a repository's `.pr_agent.toml` and comment arguments can no longer set provider endpoints (`openai.api_base` and the other `api_base` keys), keys ending in `url`, `endpoint`, `org`, `key`, `token` or `secret`, provider auth mode and TLS settings (`github.deployment_type`, `gitlab.auth_type`/`ssl_verify`, `bitbucket.auth_type`, `gitea.skip_ssl_verification`/`ssl_ca_cert`), `jira.jira_site`/`jira_api_email`/`project_keys`, or LiteLLM callbacks. They are ignored with a warning, so set them in host configuration instead. Comment arguments are restricted further as well ([#3902](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3902)). - **Gitea and Gerrit read repository settings from the target branch** ([#3906](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3906)): Gitea uses the PR base and Gerrit the default branch, so a `.pr_agent.toml` change inside a PR no longer applies to that PR. - **Cross-repository reads need an allowlist** ([#3922](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3922), [#3897](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3897)): GitHub ticket context only reads linked issues and sub-issues from the PR's own repository or same-owner repositories listed in `config.repo_context_sibling_repos`. `gitlab.expand_submodule_diffs` only expands submodules listed there that sit in the MR's top-level group. - **Ignore rules now cover comment commands** ([#3943](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3943)): `config.ignore_pr_authors`, `ignore_pr_labels`, `ignore_pr_title`, the branch rules and `ignore_repositories` now skip manually triggered commands too, not only automatic ones. - **`merge_recommendation` values were renamed** ([#4010](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/4010)): with `pr_reviewer.require_merge_recommendation` on, `safe_to_merge` is now `no_concerns_found` and `merge_with_caution` is now `needs_review`. `changes_required` is unchanged. Update anything that parses review output. - **`/describe` comments no longer repeat the PR description** ([#4118](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/4118)): with `pr_description.publish_description_as_comment = true`, the comment leaves out the User Description section even when `add_original_user_description` is on, because the PR body is left untouched. - **Smaller behaviour changes**: webhook servers reject request bodies over 5 MiB with HTTP 413 (`config.max_webhook_request_body_bytes`, [#3820](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3820)). A positive `config.max_output_tokens` below 4096 is raised to 4096 ([#4013](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/4013)). `/describe` and `/generate_labels` drop model labels outside the PR types and enabled custom labels ([#3899](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3899)). ## What's Changed ## 🚀 Features - ## ⚠️ Important Changes

- **Gitea webhooks now require a secret** ([#3637](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3637)): with `gitea.webhook_secret` unset, the Gitea app rejects every webhook with HTTP 403 instead of accepting it unsigned. Set the secret on the Gitea webhook and in your config before upgrading.
- **The GitHub Action fails on tool errors** ([#3712](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3712)): a tool failure that used to be logged and swallowed now fails the Action. Set `github_action_config.fail_on_tool_errors = false` to keep the old green behaviour.
- **Comment commands need a leading `/` on GitLab, Bitbucket and Bitbucket Server** ([#3769](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3769)): a comment only runs a tool when it starts with a slash command, so plain comments that mention one no longer trigger anything.
- **`extra_config_url` is host-only** ([#3638](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3638)): a repository's `.pr_agent.toml` can no longer set it. Configure it on the host instead, for example with `PR_AGENT_EXTRA_CONFIG_URL`.
- **`commitable_code_suggestions` is now `committable_code_suggestions`** ([#3749](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3749)): the old spelling still works with a deprecation warning until 1.0.
- **The Bitbucket Server webhook image runs under gunicorn** ([#3667](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3667)): the container now starts multiple workers through the shared `gunicorn_config.py` instead of a single Python process.

**Known issue:** Bedrock Kimi K3, new in this release ([#3651](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3651)), still receives a temperature by default, which Bedrock is reported to reject. Until [#3752](https://github.com/The-PR-Agent/pr-agent/pull/3752) lands, add the model ids to `config.no_temperature_models`.

## ⚠️ Important Changes

- **GitHub App webhooks now require a configured secret** (#2595): `get_body()` no longer accepts unsigned webhooks — a deployment without `GITHUB.WEBHOOK_SECRET` set is rejected with HTTP 403 instead of trusting every caller. Set the secret on your GitHub App and in your config before upgrading. The same PR escapes attacker-controlled webhook fields that were interpolated into CLI command strings.
- **Dependency management migrated to [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** (#2509): `requirements.txt`, `requirements-dev.txt`, and the legacy `setup.py` are gone — dependencies now live in `pyproject.toml` with a committed `uv.lock`. Set up a dev environment with `uv sync` and run tools via `uv run`. Optional features are now extras (`lambda`, `langchain` — `uv sync --extra <name>`) or a dependency group (`similar-issue` — `uv sync --group similar-issue`), and Docker images install from the lockfile with `uv sync --frozen`. Installing from PyPI with `pip install pr-agent` still works.
- **Linting consolidated on Ruff** (#2880): flake8 and the standalone isort pre-commit hook were removed. Contributors should run `uv run ruff check --fix` on touched files before committing.

body:
## ⚠️ Security

This release **temporarily disables the `/help_docs` command** as a mitigation for a credential-exposure vulnerability (#2445).

`/help_docs` accepted an untrusted runtime override of its git clone target (e.g. `--pr_help_docs.repo_url=...` from a PR comment), and the clone-URL host validation only checked substring containment. A host that merely *contained* the allowed host — e.g. `github.com.attacker.tld` — passed validation, so the git provider token was embedded into a clone URL pointing at an attacker-controlled host, exposing `GITHUB_TOKEN` (and the equivalent token on other providers).
